worksheet.title: Same and Different
worksheet.subtitle: Matching what is the same
worksheet.learning_goal: I can find the card that is the same, and the one that is different.

parts.title: Bit looks for a match
parts.text: Bit holds up a card. Help Bit find the card that is the SAME. Cards that look alike are a MATCH.

parts.title: Which one is the same as ●?
parts.note: The circle ● is the same as Bit's card. Circle the match.

parts.title: Find the same as  ★
parts.prompt: Circle the card that is the same as the star.   ●   ★   ▲

parts.title: Find the same as  ■
parts.prompt: Circle the card that is the same as the square.   ●   ▲   ■

parts.title: You try — which is different?
parts.prompt: Three are the same and one is different. Circle the one that is DIFFERENT.   ●   ●   ▲   ●

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Matching means finding what is the same. Computers match too — like finding the same face in your photos!

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children match a shape to the card that is the SAME, then spot the one that is DIFFERENT. Comparing things as same or different is a first thinking-skill behind coding — it is how computers find and group matching things. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper and a pencil or crayon. You read each prompt aloud; the child answers by circling. Optional: pairs of matching cards or objects to match by hand first.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Hold up a circle: "find the one that is the same." Point to the matching circle.
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — the star matches the star.
3. Let them try. Children do Exercise 2, then Exercise 3 (the odd one out) on their own.

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — circle the star (it matches the star). Exercise 2 — circle the square.
Exercise 3 — circle the triangle; it is different because the other three are all circles.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: circling more than one. Remind them there is exactly one match.
Make it easier: match real identical objects by hand before using the page.
Make it harder: ask "how is it different?" (shape, corners) to build describing words.
Make it active: hold up a card and have children point to its match around the room.

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children compare and match objects by attribute as they make sense of their world.
In plain terms: deciding whether two things match or are different — a first comparing skill.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child answers by drawing or circling.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child circles the one matching card each time, and finds the single different card in Exercise 3.
